text: 📸 Honestidad y resultados — Acapulco, Guerrero, 25 de septiembre de 2026

🇲🇽📚 "The best vaccine against insecurity, against crime, is education." "That hospital, do you know what money it was built with? With the sale of the presidential plane." — Presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum, Honesty and Results, Acapulco, Guerrero Guerrero is getting 22 new high schools and, in Acapulco, a Rosario Castellanos National University campus with a medical school. The new Tlapa General Hospital, left by López Obrador and finished by this government, was paid for with the sale of the presidential plane, which funded two hospitals: one in Oaxaca and one in Guerrero.

🇲🇽📜 "That is the heart of the people of Mexico: always a fighter, defending sovereignty, independence, democracy, freedom." — Presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum, Honesty and Results, Acapulco, Guerrero In Acapulco she told what came after independence: Spain did not recognize Mexico until 1836, France attacked in the Pastry War, and the United States invaded and took more than half the territory. From Guerrero, Juan N. Álvarez's Ayutla Revolution overthrew Santa Anna, and Benito Juárez, exiled to New Orleans, made his way to Acapulco to enlist as "an ordinary citizen." After the French were defeated, Juárez left the phrase: "Among individuals, as among nations, respect for the rights of others is peace."
banner: "RESPECT FOR THE RIGHTS OF OTHERS IS PEACE"

text: 🇲🇽📚 "Public school is excellent, thanks to the teachers of Mexico." "They divided the classroom into supposedly good students and bad students, those who had a scholarship and those who didn't… So in the city we changed it and gave a small scholarship to every student. You know what happened? More girls and boys have better grades, because they are recognized, because families are helped." — Presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum, Honesty and Results, Acapulco, Guerrero Critics say scholarships should go only to the top students. As head of government of Mexico City, she replaced a grant for students with a 9–10 average with a universal one. Now every public secondary student gets the Rita Cetina scholarship, and this year every public primary student got a grant for supplies and uniforms. In Guerrero, 125,149 high-school students have the Benito Juárez scholarship.

🇲🇽🏠 "They had paid for 20 years and, incredibly, they owed 500,000 pesos." "People who had requested a 50,000-peso loan, for example, had paid for 20 years and, incredibly, owed 500,000 pesos. Well, we lowered the loan for all of them, or forgave it." — Presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum, Honesty and Results, Acapulco, Guerrero More than 46,000 families in Guerrero had unpayable Infonavit and Fovissste housing loans reduced or cancelled. Nearly 51,000 Vivienda para el Bienestar homes are being built in the state for people earning two minimum wages or less, with practically no requirements to apply, and housing deeds are being regularized.

🇲🇽📜 "No, father. The homeland comes first." "His father asks Guerrero: 'Surrender, son; they are going to kill you.' And Guerrero says that phrase the people of Guerrero carry with them: 'No, father. The homeland comes first.'" — Presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum, Honesty and Results, Acapulco, Guerrero "You couldn't explain the history of Mexico without the people of Guerrero," she said in Acapulco, the municipality she has visited most since taking office. Vicente Guerrero kept the independence war going after Hidalgo and Morelos were executed and, as Mexico's second president, officially abolished slavery.

🇲🇽✊ "With great honor, I am a housewife, I am a mother, I am a grandmother and, by the will of the people of Mexico, Supreme Commander of the Armed Forces." — Presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum, Honesty and Results, Villahermosa, Tabasco Her answer to a comedian who said, when she took office, that "a housewife has reached the presidency." "Nobody should mock a housewife. Nobody," she said. "We women can be whatever we want to be. There are no limits." Women aged 60 to 64 receive the Pensión Mujeres Bienestar in recognition of the care work they have always done.
